description: Original fictional mythology and pantheon content: deities, divine families, myths, holy sites, relics, monsters and omens. Inspired-by framing only, not reconstructions of any real religion.

provenance.title: Synthetic mythology and pantheon data
provenance.creator: LexiconLang contributors
provenance.attribution: All names, stems, glosses, grammars, tables and text are original fictional content authored for LexiconLang. No deity names from living traditions, no real people, trademarks or setting-specific IP; no third-party corpora used. Forms resembling historical names were deliberately altered (for example Thor -> Vorn, Karnak -> Karnavet, Quetzalcoatl -> Quetzlcoatl).
provenance.modifications: Original invented content; no external source

tables.description: Original plot hooks for myths and legends.

result.text: A mortal stole fire and now the sky refuses rain.
A temple bell rings by itself whenever a false oath is sworn.
The river runs upstream once every nine years.
A goddess hides among mortals to learn the price of grief.
An old king bargains for one more harvest.
A star falls into the sea and the tides turn to glass.
Two brothers divide the world and disagree at the border.
A sacred tree withers on the day its keeper lies.
A monster asks for a riddle instead of a sacrifice.
A ship returns with a crew one member taller than it left with.
The moon is said to be a discarded mask.
A city forgets its own name for a single winter.
A blind singer remembers the song that made the mountains.
A child is born with the mark of an ancient wound.
The dead queue at a gate that opens only for the truthful.
An artifact surfaces in a market where no one recalls bringing it.
Every mirror in the capital shows one extra face.
The god of small things demands a festival in secret.
A hunting party finds a trail of flowers leading underground.
A oracle speaks only in the language of birds.

tables.description: Documentary-style ritual descriptions for invented traditions.

result.text: At dawn, participants wash their hands in running water and speak their true names.
A sheaf of grain is burned while the old names are recited in order.
The image is carried around the town three times before it is set down.
A silent meal is shared; no one may look at the empty chair.
A thread is tied to a branch and left until the next full moon.
A small clay boat is floated downstream carrying a written regret.
The participants turn their backs as the drum sounds twelve times.
Salt is poured in a circle; none may cross until the bell stops.
A story is told with the final line deliberately changed.
The oldest attendee lights the first lamp from the last year's ember.
Guests exchange a single word they will not use again that day.
A stone is added to the cairn, and a name is spoken only once.

tables.description: Effects of legendary artifacts in folklore.

result.text: It sweetens bitter water for one drink.
It reveals the road not taken in a single flash.
It heals a wound but takes a memory in return.
It calls the rain, though never twice in one season.
It makes the bearer invisible only while they are lying.
It turns a spoken promise into a binding mark.
It opens any lock made before the last eclipse.
It shows the face of the person who most needs forgiveness.
It grants one night of untroubled sleep.
It lets its bearer understand the speech of animals for an hour.
It multiplies a single coin, then disappears for a year.
It protects its bearer from one act of betrayal.

tables.description: 2d6 omens interpreted by fictional temple readers.

result.text: A still pool reflects a face that is not yours.
Three birds cross the sun from left to right.
An ember leaps from the hearth and dies on the threshold.
Your shadow arrives a heartbeat before you do.
Someone in the household dreams of a locked door.
A pinch of salt turns to fine white ash.
A bell sounds though no hand touched it.
Rain falls on one roof and none other.
A child loses a tooth and will not say where it went.
The ritual flame burns blue for one breath.
A mirror clouds over from the inside.
